Inclusion globs wired symmetrically on both legs with one documented order, invalid-ignored honesty, and the dead_code comment retired for inclusions only T-002
fn compile_inclusion_masks beside compile_exclusion_masks (one START_CONTRACT block, semantics documented exactly once as the extension of the exclusion canon): valid globs match against the path relative to its root, a bare glob without "/" matches the basename at any depth, "*" does not cross path separators, case-SENSITIVE (recorded v1 parity with rg's --glob default); an INVALID glob (empty/whitespace-only, NUL byte, or a glob the engine rejects) is explicitly ignored by BOTH legs — never passed to rg, never used by the walker — and increments invalid_count so the terminal forces the honest partial flag. Application order is explicit and identical on both legs, pinned in a shared comment "inclusions first, exclusions after, last match wins": the walker builds ONE combined OverrideBuilder per root adding every valid inclusion glob first and every valid exclusion mask ("!mask") after — gitignore last-match-wins semantics make exclusions sit on top of inclusions, so a path matching both is excluded; the rg transport passes each valid inclusion verbatim as a --glob= argument in the exact form format!("--glob={glob}") followed by each valid exclusion as --glob=! — the same order, the same precedence. Valid inclusions never force partial by themselves; absent or empty inclusions mean no name filter. The files-mode complete-terminal partial formula carries the #303 triggers over unchanged (an active size limit, at least one valid exclusion mask, any ignored invalid glob — exclusion or inclusion: "inclusions.invalid_count > 0" in the formula) and grows exactly one new trigger: cap_fired. Content mode is untouched: run_session, both content engine legs, build_matcher and compile_exclusion_masks keep their current behavior; inclusions remain unwired in content mode. The SearchOptions struct-level #[allow(dead_code)] attribute STAYS — leading/trailing_context_line_count are still dead — and only its comment is updated: the "inclusions globs are part of the contract but not yet wired into run_search" sentence is replaced by one naming that inclusions are wired for files mode through compile_inclusion_masks (content mode keeps ignoring them), with F-SEARCH-CONTEXT-LINES remaining the tracked dead remainder; the "not yet wired into run_search" phrasing no longer exists in the file.

FILES_RESULT_CAP = 30: prompt stop on both legs through a local cap-stop flag, the extended exit gate, and the honest complete+partial terminal T-003
One named documented constant "const FILES_RESULT_CAP: usize = 30;" — the number of the removed quick-open promise — counted on delivered path hits per session, enforced per delivered hit before emission so the delivered set never exceeds the cap exactly, including when the crossing batch overshot (the overshooting remainder is dropped, never emitted). The cap is honesty, not the count: adjusting the number would require documented rationale in this change record (the #324 precedent). The cap stop is a LOCAL flag, deliberately distinct from the shared cancel token (// START_BLOCK_FILES_CAP_STOP / // END_BLOCK_FILES_CAP_STOP): "let cap_stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));" local to the files-mode session. The walker leg breaks its entry loop on the cap and drains the pending batch; the rg files leg's read loop breaks on the cap, and BOTH the cancel watcher and the exit-status gate observe the local flag — the watcher kills and reaps the child on cancel OR cap_stop, and the gate at the "let abnormal = match status.code() {" shape is extended to "if !cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst) && !cap_stop.load(Ordering::SeqCst)" so a cap-killed rg child (signal or nonzero exit) can never surface as a false "rg exited with code N" error terminal, while a genuine exit-2 without cap or cancel still errors exactly as in #303. The shared cancel token is never written by the cap path, so run_session_files's terminal decision — which reads ONLY the shared cancel flag — completes the capped session with SearchTerminal::Complete and partial = true through the #303 additive flag; a cap is not a failure, not a cancellation, the error state is untouched, no second terminal and no cancellation is ever emitted. Test pins: the capped rg-leg session ends kind == "complete" with partial == Some(true) (never "cancelled"/"error"), zero post-terminal events; a genuine cancel during a capped-capable walk still yields exactly one cancelled terminal; and an exit-2 injected on a below-cap fixture still yields the single error terminal (the extension did not mute #303).
